_note: India festival and observance calendar, Oct 2026 to Jan 2027, plus Ganesh Chaturthi and Onam 2027. Dates were cross-checked across several panchang/calendar sources on 7 Oct 2026 (Dussehra falls on 20 or 21 Oct depending on the tithi, so both days are listed). Effects are fractional starting guesses by archetype, tuned per place by the morning tap and the owner's weights. `basis`: 'reported' = a published business source describes the direction; 'assumed' = reasoned from how the festival is observed, not measured. `regions` are states; an entry with regions only fires where the place's state is listed. `hours` are local clock hours (past 24 = after midnight).

events.name: Pitru Paksha
events.culture: Many families avoid non-veg and eating out for these 16 days; veg-forward menus hold up best.

events.name: Navratri
events.culture: Fasting thalis without onion or garlic sell; people go out every evening for garba and pandal hopping; many avoid alcohol and non-veg.

events.name: Garba nights
events.culture: Late-night crowds around garba grounds in Gujarat and Mumbai look for quick food after the dance.

events.name: Durga Puja
events.culture: Pandal hopping with family fills restaurants and street food until late; new clothes are bought beforehand.

events.name: Dussehra
events.culture: A public holiday: families go out for lunch and evening fairs; offices are shut.

events.name: Karva Chauth evening
events.culture: Couples break the fast at moonrise and many go out to dinner.

events.name: Karva Chauth grooming
events.culture: Salons and mehendi stalls are busiest in the hours before moonrise.

events.name: Dhanteras and Diwali shopping
events.basis: reported (Diwali week is the biggest revenue window); assumed (split by day)
events.culture: Buying gold, utensils and gifts is auspicious; bazaars and malls are crowded into the evening.

events.name: Diwali night
events.culture: Families are home for Lakshmi puja; shops close early; eating out picks up again from the next day.

events.name: Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj
events.culture: Siblings and extended families meet; lunches and dinners out are common.

events.name: Chhath Puja
events.culture: A strict fast kept by many families from Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP; fewer eat out.

events.name: Christmas Eve
events.culture: Dinners and parties in metros, Goa, Kerala and Northeast towns.

events.name: Christmas
events.basis: reported (some restaurants cite +30-40% on Diwali and Christmas)
events.culture: Public holiday; brunch and dinner outings, gift shopping.

events.name: New Year's Eve
events.culture: Parties and countdown dinners; bars and restaurants book out, delivery spikes after midnight.

events.name: Guru Nanak Jayanti
events.culture: Langar and processions; families go out in the evening, and many avoid alcohol. Sources differ on 24 or 25 Nov, so both days are listed.

events.name: Lohri
events.culture: Bonfire evenings with family and friends; dinners out and sweets (gajak, revri).

events.name: Makar Sankranti
events.culture: Kite flying and family lunches. Sources differ on 14 or 15 Jan, so both days are listed.

events.name: Pongal
events.culture: A harvest festival spent at home with family, then outings; new clothes beforehand. Dates differ by source, so 14 to 16 Jan are listed.

events.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
events.culture: Pandal visits and family meals; many avoid alcohol and non-veg on the first day. Only day 1 is listed; the immersion dates are not verified.

events.name: Thiruvonam
events.culture: Sadya feasts at home and big shopping beforehand; restaurants run special sadya menus. Sources differ on 12 or 13 Sep, so both days are listed.

dryDays._note: National dry days only. State dry days (festivals, elections) are not in this file; they arrive through the news signal. Source: restaurantindia.in dry-day calendar. Only archetypes that serve alcohol are affected.
